Unit Fourteen
Infinitives, Gerunds and Participles
Lesson 1: Infinitives
A. Read the following passage and look at the underlined words:

subject: English_grammar
text:
To walk early in the morning is good for health. One can get rid of
various diseases by walking regularly. It is better to walk on the riverside
or in the garden. The fresh air and the green plants are good for body
and mind. Many people walk early in the morning to keep body and
mind healthy and fresh.

subject: English_grammar
text:
[Note: These are infinitives. An infinitive is the base form of a verb but
it has different functions. ]
Look at the following examples and see how differently an_ infinitive
functions:
a) To jump is fun. (noun; subject of the verb is)
b) I like to swim. (noun; direct object of the verb /ike)

subject: English_grammar
text:
c) She had a suggestion to offer. (adjective modifying suggestion)
d) He called to warn her. (adverb modifying the verb called)
e) We decided to travel there at night. (noun; object after a transitive
verb)

subject: English_grammar
text:
Write more examples of infinitives.
[Note: the examples above are of infinitives with ‘to’]
Examples of infinitives without ‘to’:
1. They’llmeet you tomorrow. ( modal + infinitive)
2. Don’t make us laugh.
3. She let her son.take his own decision.
4. Let me conclude my opinion.
[Note: Infinitives without ‘to’ are called ‘bare infinitives’ also.]
English Grammar and Composition 125

subject: English_grammar
text: B. Read the passage below and identify ‘to+ infinitives’ and ‘bare infinitives’:

subject: English_grammar
text:
A crow was thirsty. He was flying around to find water. The day was very
hot. Water was not available anywhere. Suddenly the crow found a
pitcher. He thought there might be water in the pitcher. But the water was
at the bottom of the pitcher. The crow was wondering how to drink the
water. As he began to look around, he saw some pebbles lying on the
ground nearby. Seeing this, he thought of a way to use the pebbles to
reach the water at the bottom of the pitcher. Then the crow picked up the
pebbles with his beak and dropped them in the pitcher to make the water
rise. Soon the water level was high enough for the crow to reach. Thus he
was able to drink enough water to quench his thirst.

Lesson 2: Gerunds
A,
Read the following passage and look at the underlined words:

subject: English_grammar
text:
Swimming is a good exercise. It is also a very useful skill for safety. It is an
interesting sport. One must practice swimming to enjoy the sport. One
should not get down into water immediately after_eating. There is a
chance of drowning if you get down in water after eating. Floating on the
water is an enjoyable game. It is also an important life saving skill. This
skill may save us from drowning. It is necessary to learn swimming by
taking help of a trainer.

subject: English_grammar
text:
Note: These are gerunds. A gerund is the present participle form of a verb
(verb+ ing) which works like a noun.
126 English Grammar and Composition
B. Read the passage below and underline the gerunds:

subject: English_grammar
text:
Travelling is a good practice to acquire knowledge and experience. Visiting
many places, we can be familiar with different geographical and cultural
features. Those who travel for sight-seeing prefer to visit places which are
unusual to them. They may go hiking or sailing. In our country the winter
season is best for travelling. Driving long in this season is comfortable and
Safe.

subject: English_grammar
text:
A gerund can take different positions in a sentence.
Look at the following sentences:
e Eating much is harmful.
e Driving too fast is dangerous.
e Walking is a good exercise for everybody.
e Her_knitting is beautiful.
In these sentences, the gerund is the subject.
A gerund can be used as the object in the sentence.

subject: English_grammar
text:
For example:
e | didn’t mind joining the music competition.
e She likes sleeping in the afternoon.
e | enjoy reading and writing.
e He finished playing at 9 o’clock.
Gerund after preposition:
1. | have no objection to walking.
2. She is fond of shopping.
C. Make sentences with the following gerunds:

subject: English_grammar
text:
Dancing (as subject), praying (after a preposition), watching (as object),
shocking (as object), meeting (as subject), sleeping (after a preposition),
fasting (as subject), surfing (as subject), typing (as object), closing (after a
preposition).

Lesson 3: Participles
A. Read the following passage and look at the underlined words in different
positions:

subject: English_grammar
text:
The_dancing peacock displayed his feathers. The people who gathered
there enjoyed the show. Peacocks are found displaying feathers when it
rains. So it is a rare opportunity to see a peacock dancing and displaying
feathers. Peacocks are found dancing in the open space in front of the
forest. We are charmed by their dancing.

subject: English_grammar
text:
Note: These are participles. A participle is a verb that ends in ing (present
participle) or ed, d, t, en, n (past participle). Participles may function as
adjectives describing or modifying nouns. See more examples:
The talking parrots entertained the crowd. (present participle)
The wrecked sailboat washed up on shore. (past participle)

subject: English_grammar
text:
Note: But participles have another function. When used with helping verbs
such as to be and to have, they are action verbs and form several verb
tenses.
Example:
1. She is thinking of the children.
2. The conference room had been cleaned before they arrived.
3. The job has been_done successfully.
